content:
I found something curious when looking at the declaration diff report of #40732 (version bump to v4.32.0-rc1)

-Nat.lt_succ_sqrt
-Nat.sqrt.iter_sq_le
-Nat.sqrt.lt_iter_succ_sq
-Nat.sqrt_le
+Subtype.eq_iff

The first four about sqrt are expected as they were moved from Mathlib to core. The last one is interesting. It got "introduced" at docs#Subtype.eq_iff (guess the file name before clicking it)

The actual code is

set_option linter.deprecated false in  -- this line was added in the version bump
attribute [local ext] Subtype.eq -- this line has been there for three years

I wonder what caused this apparent declaration change?
It existed in core and was deleted in lean#13955
Oh! so the [ext] attribute now generates a new eq_def because the one from core no longer exists
Kim Morrison deprecated it in lean#10967, because Subtype.eq is considered a duplicate of Subtype.ext, see #mathlib4 > duplicate declarations @ 💬
Since Subtype.eq & Subtype.eq_iff have been deprecated for more than 6 months, does that mean that Mathlib is no longer using it and we can just delete this? Nice catch btw!

As a side effect mathlib users now have an undeprecated Subtype.eq_iff (idk why the local in local ext doesn't work), so we should delete it soon to avoid a second deprecation cycle.
Also Subtype.eq should probably be deleted from core.
To answer your question: the local refers just to the ext tag, i.e. it is only locally used in the ext tactic. Though I agree it would make sense if the local also made the _iff theorem private.
I can work on cleaning this up

#40867
Seems to work for the file locally by just removing the two lines. Let's see if it breaks anything else in Mathlib
I wonder what was the reason for set_option linter.deprecated false in attribute [local ext] Subtype.eq though.
The local ext attribute was added over 3 years ago in #3332. I might have been necessary then, or it was just an oversight.
